uncertain.why: Under the stacked ta-ha ligature of «الفاتحين» only one kasra is printed. It sits under the ta and the right part of the ha (checked at 3600 dpi). This font puts the below-marks of stacked ligature parts at the same spot: compare the lam kasra in «وَالكَلِمَاتِ» and the mim kasra in «الْعَالَمِينَ». So it could be two kasras (ta and ha) printed on top of each other, or a single kasra on the ta or on the ha. In the ha-mim ligature of «الرَّاحِمِينَ» (p.084), which is side by side and not stacked, two separate kasras show. Every other word in this dua is fully vowelled, so the best reading has both kasras.

Same case in the stacked lam-mim ligature: only one kasra is printed under «لم» (checked at 3500 dpi), and it could be the lam's kasra and the mim's kasra on top of each other. The best reading follows the fully vowelled pattern of the dua (الرَّازِقِينَ، الغَافِرِينَ، النَّاصِرِينَ).

keyA.notes:
Markers: p.081 opens a new section (# المسبعات العشر). p.080 ends with the complete «[الصافات: ١٨٠-١٨٢].» and has no footnotes, so there is no + and no (تابع). p.082 opens with a new item (### ٧- الباقيات الصالحات) and p.083 with a new section (# حزب البحر), so neither gets a +. p.083 ends «…وَارْحَمْنَا» and p.084 continues «فَإِنَّكَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ», so it is <<<ص:084+>>>. There are no footnotes anywhere in the batch.

The Quran span 55:19-20 runs past the end of p.084 (the page ends «…بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ»). Following b17/b18/b19/b27, I closed it with ﴾ at the page end; p.085 will reopen ﴿ before «لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ (٢٠)».

Headings and bold: STRUCTURE fixes the # headings «المسبعات العشر» and «حزب البحر» and the ### heading «الصلاة الإبراهيمية». «٦- آية الكرسي» and «٧- الباقيات الصالحات» are set in the same bold title font, centred on their own line, like «الصلاة الإبراهيمية», so they are ### too, with their printed numbers. Items ١-٥ on p.081 are in the same large bold font but set flush right (all start at the same indent) and are instructions, not titles. They contrast with the regular Quran text on the page, so each is a bold paragraph «**١-سورة الفاتحة (سبع مرات)**». Every «(سبع مرات)» at a line end on pp.081-082 is bold against regular text, so it is written **(سبع مرات)** in the same paragraph, after the text it ends. The lines under the titles («(تقرأ يوميا …)», «لسيدي أبي الحسن الشاذلي (رضي الله عنه)», «(يقرأ مرَّة يوميًّا منفردًا)», «يقرأ في جماعة …») are plain paragraphs per STRUCTURE §2, even though they are set in a heavier face. The رضي الله عنه glyph is written (رضي الله عنه). The calligraphic basmala on p.083 is written as the standard line, outside brackets.

Spacing, measured at 600 dpi (a word space is about 49-61 px in the p.081 list): item ١-٤ «N-سورة» has no space after the hyphen (13-14 px) and item ٥ «٥- سورة» has one (51 px). Items ٢ and ٤ put «(» only 24 px after the word, against 55-61 px in items ١, ٣ and ٥, so they are «الناس(سبع» and «الإخلاص(سبع». The p.081 subtitle is a tightly set bold font in which every word gap is narrow, so it is written with normal single spaces. «[طه:١١١]» is printed with no space after the colon, while the other references have one. «طسٓ-حمٓ- عٓسٓقٓ» has no space around the first hyphen and a space only after the second (gap 24 px, the same as the word space after «،»). Printed dashes are written as the ASCII '-'. A space is written between ﴾ and [ as in the earlier batches. The muqatta'at «كٓهيعٓصٓ», «طسٓ», «حمٓ», «عٓسٓقٓ» are in the ordinary font outside ﴿﴾, so they are plain text with each printed madda (U+0653): on ك, ع and ص; on س; on م; and on ع, س and ق.

Printed-vowel details, checked at 1500-4000 dpi: «أَنْتَ» ×2 has the nun's sukun overlapping the alif's hamza and fatha. «وَزُلْزِلُواْ» has a sukun on the silent alif. «زِلْزَالاً» puts the fathatan over the alif arm of the lam-alif, «شَدِيدًا» puts it on the dal, «عاجلاً/وآجلاً» put it over the alif, and «ثلاثًا» puts it on the tha. In the dua the article's lam is mostly unvowelled (الحَسْبُ، العَزِيزُ، المُؤْمِنُونَ، لِلقُلُوبِ، المُضِيَّ، المَجِيءَ …), and that is kept. «السَّلامَةِ» ×2, «فَلا» and «وَلا» have no vowel on the lam-alif, while «الْعَالَمِينَ» (p.082) does carry a sukun on the lam. Plain «الله» is used where only the ligature's automatic marks show (p.082). Final ى with the automatic Lotus small alif is written plain (عَلَى، لِمُوسَى).

Quran (2:255, 33:12, 36:66-67, 36:1-9, 20:111, 55:19-20): every word was read from the image. The round zero on the silent alif of «فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟/ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟» is ۟ (it differs from the khaa-head sukun). The small high mim in «مِنۢ» is ۢ. Neither the rub' sign ۞ of 20:111 nor the basmala of Ya-Sin is printed, so neither is included. scripts/quran.py reports no flags, and validate.py prints OK. Harakat order was normalized to shadda first.

uncertain.why: Only one kasra is printed under the vertical ta-ha ligature of الفاتحين; it sits under the ta, so the kasra on ha seems omitted. Two exactly overlapping kasras cannot be fully ruled out (then الفَاتِحِينَ).
Only one kasra is printed under the vertical lam-mim ligature of الظالمين, nearer the lam stroke, so the kasra on mim seems omitted. Overlapping kasras cannot be fully ruled out (then الظَّالِمِينَ).

keyB.notes: p.081 is not a continuation: p.080 ends with a complete Quran quotation and its reference. Items ١–٧ of المسبعات العشر (including «٦- آية الكرسي» and «٧- الباقيات الصالحات») are written as bold paragraphs, following STRUCTURE's «numbered list (bold)», not as ### headings. «الصلاة الإبراهيمية» is ### per STRUCTURE. The spacing after the hyphen is kept as printed: «١-سورة» to «٤-سورة» have none, while «٥- سورة» and «٦- آية» have a space. The subtitle lines under the titles («(تقرأ يوميا …)», «(يقرأ مرَّة يوميًّا منفردًا)», «يقرأ في جماعة …») are plain paragraphs per STRUCTURE, though printed bold. The «(سبع مرات)» at the end of a line, separated by a wide gap, is bold and kept in the same paragraph. On p.083 the calligraphic basmala is written in its standard form outside the brackets. «كٓهيعٓصٓ» on p.083 and «طسٓ-حمٓ- عٓسٓقٓ» on p.084 are in the ordinary font with no ﴿﴾, so they are ordinary text with their printed maddas (U+0653). The dash spacing «طسٓ-حمٓ- عٓسٓقٓ» was measured from pixel gaps. «[طه:١١١]» is printed with no space after the colon. The fathatan on a lam-alif ligature is written after the alif («زِلْزَالاً», «عاجلاً وآجلاً»), because the print cannot show which letter carries it. «وَزُلْزِلُواْ» has a printed sukun on the alif. In the dua text the qamari lam usually has no sukun (e.g. «لِلقُلُوبِ», «المُؤْمِنُونَ», «الحَسْبُ»), except «فِي الْعَالَمِينَ» on p.082, which has one. The lam-alif in «السَّلامَةِ», «فَلا» and «وَلا» has no fatha, as printed. p.084 is a continuation (+) of the كهيعص paragraph. «شَاهَتِ الوُجُوهُ (ثلاثًا).» is not indented and follows a nearly full line, so it is kept in the same paragraph as the Yasin passage. The Quran quotation of al-Rahman 19–20 runs onto p.085: per the earlier keyB practice (b18), it is closed with ﴾ after «بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ» at the end of p.084, so p.085 should reopen with ﴿. Quran spans cross-checked with scripts/quran.py: no flags.
